Writing your own warm-up patterns

In Vocal Ladder, an exercise is written as numbers: the degrees of the scale, counted from Do. Because the numbers do not name actual notes, the same pattern works in every key, and the app moves it up or down for you.

Numbers are scale degrees

1 is Do, the note of the key. 2 to 7 are Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, and Ti of the major scale, and 8 is Do an octave up. Separate the notes with spaces. So Do-Re-Mi-Fa-Sol-Fa-Mi-Re-Do is 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 1.

Each number is one beat at the tempo you set. Add - to make a note longer: 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 1- holds the last Do for two beats.

Everything you can write

WriteMeaningPlayed in the key of C4
1 2 3 4 5 6 7Do Re Mi Fa Sol La Ti of the keyC4, D4, E4, F4, G4, A4, B4
8 9 10 12The next octave: 8 is Do, 9 Re, 10 Mi … up to 15C5, D5, E5, G5
b3 #4b before a number: a half step lower. # before a number: a half step higherEb4, F#4
5, 1'“,” after a number: an octave lower. “'”: an octave higherG3, C5
1- 1--Each “-” after a note makes it one beat longerC4 (2 beats), C4 (3 beats)
1/ 1//Each “/” after a note makes it half as longC4 (0.5 beats), C4 (0.25 beats)
1 r 1r is a rest (it can take - and / too). A pattern needs at least one note to singC4, rest, C4

Up to two octaves above or below Do. If the app cannot read something, it shows what it could not read, and Start stays off until it is fixed.

“One key” is the 2-beat chord plus the melody. The next key's chord comes right after it.

Examples of your own patterns

  • 1 3 5 3 1 3 5 3 1- – Do-Mi-Sol twice, for longer breath. In the key of C4: C4 E4 G4 E4 C4 E4 G4 E4 C4; 12 beats per key.
  • 5 4 3 2 1 2 3 4 5 4 3 2 1- – Sol down to Do and back, then down again. In the key of C4: G4 F4 E4 D4 C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 F4 E4 D4 C4; 16 beats per key.
  • 1/ 2/ 3/ 4/ 5/ 4/ 3/ 2/ 1--- – A quick five-note run with a long last note. In the key of C4: C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 F4 E4 D4 C4; 10 beats per key.
  • 1 b3 5 b3 1- – Do-Mi♭-Sol: a minor arpeggio (the chord before each key is minor too). In the key of C4: C4 Eb4 G4 Eb4 C4; 8 beats per key.

To keep one, tap Save this pattern and give it a name. It is added at the top of the pattern list for every set and exercise. See the guide.

Tips

  • Ending: holding the last note for 2 beats (1-) gives you a moment before the next key's chord.
  • Bars: if the beats of one key, including the 2-beat chord, add up to a multiple of 4, every key starts on the first beat of a bar. Most built-in patterns do.
  • Minor: a pattern with b3 and no 3 gets a minor chord before each key.
  • Range: the pattern's lowest and highest notes decide the range you sing. Check the range shown under the start and end keys before you start.

Warm up with a piano that climbs with you

Choose an exercise, the start and end keys, and the tempo. The piano moves it up or down a half step at a time. Free, no sign-up, and it works offline.
